title: Japanese/English Exchange group ENKAI（縁会）
description:
日本語と英語で話そう！Let's join Japanese/English Exchange group ENKAI（縁会）!

Learn Japanese/English, make friends, learn about culture!All Levels Welcome!Are you looking for opportunities to practice your Japanese or English? Have fun meeting new people while practicing your target language with native speakers. Plus, you get to return the favor and help others reach their goal to become fluent in another language! Not only will you walk away feeling like you've improved your English or Japanese, but you'll also feel great about helping someone else reach his or her goals. Let's enjoy ENKAI!

Fee: $11 to be paid at the counter (Includes regular flat white, coffee, tea, or a fizzy drink)

title: EMC English Conversation Club
description:
**EMC English Conversation Club**
**Thursdays, 4 to 6pm**
**Free.** Please **join this group** and **reserve** your seat every week.

Whether you want to improve your English or you're a native speaker keen to help others, this is a great place to connect and build friendships.
This is not a classroom. It’s a relaxed community space where you can share stories, practise everyday English, and learn about life, work, and culture in New Zealand and other countries.
Each session is guided by an experienced facilitator and supported by friendly volunteers.

• Casual, friendly conversations on real-life topics

• Language learning through connection, not pressure
• A welcoming environment to build friendships and confidence

Please **join this group** and **reserve** your seat every week.

title: Footnote (Israel, 2012, 1 hr 47 mins)
description:
One of the absurdities of the crazy war in the Middle East is that Israel, Iran and Palestine all produce well made films that depict beautifully the human condition with all our complexities. loves and frailties and or common humanity. In our film club we have seen these films. How can humans possibly fight each other? Why?

In this tragi-comic film, a father and son are both professors at the same university in Jerusalem. They have a classic love/hate relationship. We don't necessarily end up siding with either of them, as neither really gain our full sympathy. But we "get" them and that is the genius of the film.

Some reviews:
“Footnote requires little knowledge of Judaism and its texts. Rather, it's about the complications of love, guilt, and rage.” The New Yorker
It's not easy to make Eliezer a sympathetic character, yet Bar-Aba's demonstration of fleeting vulnerability awakens inevitable, if equally brief, compassion.” Washington Post
“This is brainy, bravura filmmaking of the highest level, a motion picture that is as difficult to pigeonhole as it is a pleasure to enjoy.” Los Angeles Times
“Shows just what you can do with a carefully constructed plot and lovingly drawn characters - even if, in the end, neither of them is particularly lovable.” London Evening Standard

Nominated for an Oscar as Best Foreign Language Film and won the prize for screenplay at Cannes
